title: Restaurant Review Sentiment with VADER
description:
A lightweight Python tool that reads restaurant reviews from a CSV file and reports how positive or negative they are, overall and per topic: food, service, ambience, price, waiting time and cleanliness.

  • VADER (via the vaderSentiment package) scores each review from -1 to 1. It is rule-based, ships its lexicon inside the package, needs no training data and no API key, and handles negation ("not good"), intensifiers and capital letters.
  • A small restaurant lexicon adds words VADER treats as neutral, such as "overpriced", "bland" or "slow".
  • Reviews are split into clauses (at sentence ends and words such as "but"); each clause that mentions a topic keyword gives that topic its score, so "great food but noisy" counts as positive for food and negative for ambience.
  • The report lists counts and shares of positive, neutral and negative reviews, per-topic averages and the most negative reviews to read first.
implementationSteps: Export reviews to a CSV file with one review per row (for example from your review platform or booking system).
Install the only dependency: pip install -r requirements.txt.
Run python -m reviews reviews.csv --out-csv results.csv --out-json report.json.
Each review gets VADER's compound score, labeled positive (>= 0.05), negative (<= -0.05) or neutral.
Clauses that mention topic keywords give per-topic scores; adjust the keyword lists in ASPECTS for your menu and venue.
Add words that matter for your reviews to DOMAIN_LEXICON and re-run.
Read the most negative reviews and the topics with the highest negative share first, and track the shares month by month.
performance:
Expectations, not measured results:

  • Thousands of reviews per second on a laptop; no GPU, no network.
  • VADER is built for short English texts. Mixed reviews are its weak spot: it weights the clause after "but" more, so "amazing food, but noisy" comes out negative overall while the topic scores still show the positive food rating.
  • Check agreement with star ratings on a sample of your own reviews. If it is too low, train a classifier (for example scikit-learn on labeled reviews) or use a transformer sentiment model.
userExperience: The owner runs one command and gets a JSON report (shares of positive, neutral and negative reviews, a score per topic and the most negative reviews) plus a CSV with the score of every review that opens in a spreadsheet. Charts can be built from the CSV in any spreadsheet tool.
